title: Windows Checkout Illegal Filenames
description: Dev cannot check out the repo on Windows because tracked paths contain Windows-illegal filename components (e.g. a whitespace-only filename inside a ticket folder). Audit all tracked paths for Windows-illegal components (forbidden chars <>:"|?*, control chars, trailing space/dot, leading space, reserved device names CON/PRN/AUX/NUL/COM#/LPT#, empty/whitespace-only names), remove or rename the offenders, and make sure `bun ./📜️script.ts clean` (the workspace `windows-illegal` removal kind already implemented in 📜️script.ts) actually detects and deletes any such paths going forward, including inside open (non-closed) tickets.
summary: Audited all 72772 tracked paths twice (independent scan + the real cleanIsWindowsIllegalName imported straight from 📜️script.ts): 0 Windows-illegal filenames exist right now, and no case-insensitive collisions either. Confirmed clean's existing windows-illegal removal already really deletes (git rm -f, bypasses ticket-open protection) rather than just reporting, so no code change was warranted for the described symptom. The actual likely blocker for the Windows checkout is path length: 204 tracked paths would exceed Win32's 260-char MAX_PATH with a modest checkout root, some up to 293 UTF-16 units, mostly legitimate deep taxonomy-driven content (norm/DIN16798 fixtures) or debris in two open tickets (SEMANTIC-MUTATIONS-OVERHAUL, ENFORCE-UNIQUE-SEMANTIC-EMOJIS-ACROSS-REPOSITORY) that this session did not touch since one was being actively written to by another session. Recommended fix is non-destructive: enable `git config core.longpaths true` + Windows LongPathsEnabled, not deleting/renaming legitimate content. Findings and scan scripts kept in this ticket folder. repo/semio MCP failed to connect this session (dispatcher verified alive via `client entity-emojis`); ticket bookkeeping done by hand on disk.
